idiom_name: identity data member + libpqxx RETURNING / sqlite3_last_insert_rowid() read-back
implementation_notes: In hand-written C++ the identity field is a data member (std::int64_t or a UUID type) and the mapper reads the key back from the statement - libpqxx exposes the RETURNING row as a result tuple, sqlite3_last_insert_rowid() covers SQLite - or generates it in the application with a UUID library when it must exist before the INSERT. The classic key-generator object is replaced by the SQL schema (identity/serial column) plus that statement-level read. Keep the hand-written form while the project binds SQL itself; the ODB compiler is the alternative that moves the whole mapping into pragmas on the class. Never write UPDATE ... WHERE name = ? - target the identity member.
pitfalls: 0 means 'not yet persisted' but is also a valid-looking value: keeping the sentinel in the mapper avoids treating an unsaved object as row 0.
A pooled connection must not be swapped between the INSERT and the key read-back; read RETURNING (or last_insert_rowid) on the same connection and transaction that ran the insert.
Narrowing the key to int or passing it to printf-style logging with %d silently corrupts large ids - carry std::int64_t end to end.

variants.name: ODB persistent class (#pragma db id auto)
variants.idiom_name: #pragma db id auto on the identity member
variants.implementation_notes: ODB declares identity inside the class: the pragma '#pragma db id auto' before the member tells the ODB compiler that this member is the object's identifier and that the database assigns it, after which libodb plus libodb-<database> generate load/insert/update/delete and the key read-back. Omitting 'auto' keeps the identifier application-assigned (for example a UUID string). Choose ODB when persistent classes may carry pragmas and the build can run the ODB compiler; it replaces both the hand-written binding and the manual key read-back.
pitfalls: Mixing hand-written INSERTs with the generated ODB runtime gives the same class two notions of 'new': always persist and update through the generated API.
The pragma-declared key is still 0 until persist() runs, and 0 is not a value the database would generate, so a default-constructed object must not be treated as persisted.
The ODB compiler is a build step: generated code must be regenerated whenever the pragmas or members change, or the mapping silently drifts from the class.
